content.comment_body: If the password for [product_name] access is set, then connecting to [product_name] requires the password. You can't reset the password without knowing the previously set password.

If the password for [product_name] access is set, connecting via the Tools menu will require entering the password. However, if you try via the File menu, it may not ask for the password—you can test this yourself and share the outcome.

It prompts for the password. Try closing [product_name] and reopening, then attempt to activate File > Properties > Online access > Connect. The program password is different from the access password. If you don’t switch to operator mode from admin mode, you can reset to factory settings through the [product_name] menu if your device has a display. But if you've switched to operator mode and don’t know the admin or access passwords, you’re locked out. Loading an empty program via SD card doesn’t remove the access password.
Apologies, after a retest it also requires entering the access password. Perhaps cached data occasionally bypasses the password prompt.

This isn’t how industrial-grade equipment should function, right? You’d expect a more refined product from [company_name] compared to hobbyist devices. Certificate management for newer [product_name] versions is another issue—[company_name] uses its own CA certificates trusted by browsers, but for some reason, there’s a self-signed certificate involved that requires manual installation for secure browser access.

Let’s avoid going off topic, as it’s closely regulated here. I’ve been impressed by [product_name] since using older versions years ago. Now, newer versions are more affordable and have more features. I’m hoping for significant improvements, bug fixes, and essential features in future releases. Perhaps we’ll write a 'wish list' for the upcoming version soon. Just my opinion.

If you've set both the access and admin mode passwords and forgot them (or don’t have access), you cannot perform a factory reset unless [product_name] is in admin mode. 1) Via display: Without the admin password, you can’t set your device to admin mode if it’s in operator mode, and only in admin mode can you switch to STOP, which reveals the menu entry for 'Factory Reset'. 2) Via software: Without the access password, you can’t connect, nor select the factory reset option in [product_name] software. One workaround is transferring an empty program via an SD card, then restarting the device; it will remain in STOP mode. However, the factory reset entry isn’t available without the operator password. In summary: you cannot perform a factory reset if both passwords have been set and are unknown.

Having lived all my life in Eastern Europe, maybe I’m less diplomatic—someone has to point out the obvious, or nothing changes. I’m willing to pay extra for quality. Older [product_name] units had limitations, but they were reliable year after year, until the hardware failed or was replaced. You can convert old programs for newer [product_name] models, and even the first version from 1996 is still supported, which is great. But you can’t be sure everything will work perfectly—some functions reportedly behave inconsistently on new devices. For future versions, whether it’s 9.0 or 8.X, you won’t just replace all installed devices because there’s a newer release. Software always comes with bugs, but ignoring feedback from engineers and not releasing fixes is unacceptable. It’s hard to trust repeated claims of 'forwarded to the development team' or 'works here' if no visible improvements appear. My main wish for new versions: fix known bugs for older devices via firmware updates.

I understand your frustrations, but please avoid expressing them on unrelated topics. Consider starting your own thread, for example: 'What bothers me about [product_name] hardware and software,' and share your concerns there—preferably not in other threads. Thanks.

I was responding to another thread just now, but point taken—I’ll watch for any reaction from [company_name]. Maybe past large-scale failures will serve as a lesson for management. Despite issues, I still appreciate the ideas behind [product_name] and the clarity of its logic when creating diagrams. Compared to other brands, it’s unmatched.
Sorry, but I don't support posting unrelated frustrations in other topics.

analysis.insight_summary: Users highlight a major usability problem with password management on [product_name] devices, particularly in cases where both admin and access passwords are lost, making factory resets impossible and locking out authorized users. While users accept the need for security, the inability to recover or reset the device without original passwords results in operational difficulties and irritation. Feedback also points to inconsistent feature reliability between versions and persistent software bugs, diminishing confidence in long-term support and manufacturer responsiveness.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a secure but feasible method for factory reset or recovery in cases where passwords are unknown, as well as stable, bug-free performance across multiple generations of [product_name]. Improved technical support and continued maintenance for older models are also desired.
